expectations.text: States survivability-enhanced aircraft moved off USML Category VIII(a)(8) effective October 13, 2026 (interim final rule, 91 FR 55457)
expectations.evidence: Explicitly disclaims knowledge of the rule: "My reference material does not include any October 2026 rule on aircraft or countermeasure jurisdiction." No VIII(a)(8), October 13, 2026, or 91 FR 55457.

expectations.text: States the modified aircraft are now subject to the EAR (Commerce jurisdiction)
expectations.evidence: "The airliner itself, as an FAA type-certificated civil aircraft, would normally remain under the EAR... Installing ITAR-controlled equipment does not by itself move the airframe to the ITAR" (though framed under the pre-existing regime, not the new rule).

expectations.text: States the secured aircraft survivability equipment itself (DIRCM plus associated IR/UV missile warning with anti-tamper) remains on the USML in Category XI(a)(4)
expectations.evidence: Says only "for example Category XI and the aircraft category VIII... and Category XII" and admits "I am not certain which paragraph covers a given configuration." Never identifies XI(a)(4).

expectations.text: Mentions the conditions: in-production manned civil aircraft with FAA transport/commuter type certificate or NATO/MNNA equivalent, with definitions added at 22 CFR 121.0
expectations.evidence: No mention of the transport/commuter type-certificate condition, NATO/MNNA equivalents, or the new definitions at 22 CFR 121.0.

expectations.text: Does not assert that the rule assigned a specific destination ECCN (the rule names none)
expectations.evidence: Never claims the rule assigned an ECCN; 9A991/9A610 are offered only as typical pre-existing classifications, with the caveat that classification "must be analyzed separately."
